salmanshh_platformer_navigationgraph.name: Platformer Navigation Graph
salmanshh_platformer_navigationgraph.description: Smart pathfinding for platformer games. Characters automatically jump across gaps, fall between platforms, and find optimal routes through complex levels. Includes instant portals (teleporters, doors) and gradual portals (elevators, ladders, ziplines) with pause/resume support for custom animations. Features hazard avoidance, multiple path strategies, coyote jumps, ledge restriction, and multi-agent support. Works with the built-in Platform behavior — just add the behavior and go.

enable_debug.name: Enable Debug Logging
enable_debug.desc: Show helpful debug messages in browser console (F12) to troubleshoot pathfinding issues. Disable for better performance in final game.

cell_size.name: Tile Size
cell_size.desc: Size of each grid tile in pixels. MUST match the Cell Size in your Pathfinding behavior! Smaller = more precise paths but slower performance.

max_search_nodes.name: Max Search Nodes
max_search_nodes.desc: Maximum pathfinding effort before giving up. Higher = finds paths in larger levels but may cause lag. Lower = faster but may fail on complex paths.

max_fall_distance.name: Max Fall Distance
max_fall_distance.desc: Maximum fall distance in pixels. 0 = auto-detect from Platform behavior. -1 = unlimited (any fall). Positive value = custom max in pixels.

auto_control.name: Auto-Control Movement
auto_control.desc: When enabled, AI automatically controls the character (moves left/right, jumps). When disabled, you handle movement yourself using the path data.

graph_mode.name: Graph Mode
graph_mode.desc: How navigation data is stored. Shared = all characters use same map (efficient). Per-Instance = each character has own map (rare use cases only).

path_strategy.name: Path Strategy
path_strategy.desc: How the AI picks the best route when multiple paths exist. Balanced: weighs distance and difficulty equally, good for most platformers and adventure games. Shortest Distance: always takes the fastest route even with risky jumps, ideal for speedrunner games and time trials. Safest Route: avoids jumps and falls when possible, great for stealth games, escort missions, or fragile NPCs. Simplest Path: fewest waypoints for predictable movement, best for simple enemies and tower defense creeps.

smooth_paths.name: Smooth Paths
smooth_paths.desc: Remove unnecessary waypoints for more natural movement. AI will take direct routes when possible instead of zigzagging.

max_waypoint_time.name: Max Waypoint Time
max_waypoint_time.desc: How long (in seconds) AI tries to reach each waypoint before giving up and recalculating path. Prevents infinite loops when stuck.

coyote_time.name: Coyote Time
coyote_time.desc: Seconds after walking off a ledge where a jump can still be executed. Allows AI to walk off edges and jump mid-air for greater reach, making slightly out-of-range platforms reachable. Important: only works when 'Ledge Restriction' is disabled — if Ledge Restriction is enabled, characters won't walk off edges, so coyote jumps can never execute and the connections will go unused. 0 = disabled.

strict_positioning.name: Strict Jump Positioning
strict_positioning.desc: When the AI is following a path and needs to jump or fall to another platform, it will slow down and carefully position itself on the tile before launching. This prevents characters from overshooting edges and missing jumps — like a chase enemy flying off a ledge instead of jumping across, or an escort NPC slipping off a narrow bridge mid-jump. Note: this only affects movement DURING pathfinding (jumps and falls that are part of the path). To stop characters from walking off edges entirely, use 'Ledge Restriction' instead. Recommended ON for most games.

ledge_restriction.name: Ledge Restriction
ledge_restriction.desc: Prevents AI characters from walking off platform edges when they have no reason to leave. Useful for patrol guards that should stay on their platform, or NPCs that shouldn't wander off rooftops. Note: this only stops characters from casually walking off edges — if the AI's path requires a jump or fall to reach its goal, it will still leave the platform. When enabled, 'Coyote Time' has no effect since characters won't walk off edges to trigger it. When disabled, characters can slide off edges freely, which also enables wall-adjacent jumps (walking to the platform edge to clear a wall before jumping). To make jumps and falls more precise, use 'Strict Jump Positioning' instead.

ledge_leniency.name: Ledge Leniency
ledge_leniency.desc: How many pixels past a platform edge the AI is allowed to walk before stopping (0 = strict stop at edge). Increase for more natural-looking movement near edges. Only used when Ledge Restriction is enabled.

repath_threshold.name: Re-Path Threshold
repath_threshold.desc: How many tiles the character can deviate from its path before automatically recalculating. Useful when the character gets knocked off course. 0 = disabled.

hazard_radius.name: Hazard Radius
hazard_radius.desc: Tile radius for hazard cost falloff buffer zone. Nearby tiles within this radius of a hazard get cost penalties. 0 = no buffer, only exact hazard tiles affected.

SetMaxFallDistance.display-text: Set max fall distance to {0} px
SetMaxFallDistance.description: Override the auto-calculated maximum fall distance. The navigation graph must be regenerated after changing this for the new value to take effect.

SetMaxJumpDistance.display-text: Set max jump distance to {0} px
SetMaxJumpDistance.description: Override the auto-calculated maximum horizontal jump distance. The navigation graph must be regenerated after changing this for the new value to take effect.

SetMaxJumpHeight.display-text: Set max jump height to {0} px
SetMaxJumpHeight.description: Override the auto-calculated maximum jump height. The navigation graph must be regenerated after changing this for the new value to take effect.

LogGraphStats.display-text: Log navigation graph statistics to console
LogGraphStats.description: Output detailed navigation graph statistics to the browser console. Use for debugging graph generation and connectivity issues.

AddCircleHazard.description: Add a circular hazard area. The AI will avoid this area based on severity. Hazard avoidance is automatically enabled. Returns a hazard ID for later removal. Use for dynamic danger zones like explosions or enemy AOE.

AddRectHazard.description: Add a rectangular hazard area. The AI will avoid this area based on severity. Hazard avoidance is automatically enabled. Returns a hazard ID for later removal. Use for static danger zones like spike pits.

ClearAllHazards.display-text: Clear all circle and rectangle hazards
ClearAllHazards.description: Remove all circular and rectangular hazards. This does NOT clear tile-based hazards. Use when resetting a level or clearing all dynamic dangers.

ClearAllHazardTiles.description: Reset all tile hazard severities to 0. This does NOT remove circle/rect hazards. Use when you want to clear static tile dangers.

RemoveHazard.description: Remove a hazard by its ID. Use this when a danger zone is no longer active. The graph will be regenerated if needed.

BuildObstacleMapFromLayout.description: Create an empty obstacle map grid from layout pixel dimensions. No Pathfinding behavior required. Follow with ScanSolidObjectsIntoObstacleMap and ScanJumpThruObjectsIntoObstacleMap to fill it.

ClearAllSlopes.description: Remove all slope markings from the obstacle map. Slopes will be treated as regular solid tiles. Use this to reset slope data.

ClearObstacleMap.description: Remove the obstacle map and all associated data. Use this when switching levels or resetting the navigation system.

CreateCustomObstacleMap.display-text: Create custom obstacle map [Width: {0} tiles] [Height: {1} tiles]
CreateCustomObstacleMap.description: Create a custom obstacle map with the specified dimensions in tiles. All tiles are initialized to 'clear' state. Use this when not using the Pathfinding behavior's obstacle map.

GenerateNodesFromCustomMap.display-text: Generate navigation graph from obstacle map
GenerateNodesFromCustomMap.description: Generate the navigation graph from the current obstacle map. Call this after setting up all tiles and before pathfinding. This is an expensive operation.

LoadObstacleMapFromJSON.description: Load a previously saved obstacle map from JSON string. Use this to restore saved maps or load pre-built level data.

json.name: JSON
json.desc: JSON string containing obstacle map data

MapSlopeTilesFromTilemap.display-text: Map slopes from {0}: left={1} right={2} gentle-left={3} gentle-right={4}
MapSlopeTilesFromTilemap.description: Scan a Tilemap and mark tiles matching the given tile IDs as slopes. Pass tile IDs as comma-separated strings (e.g. '5,6,7'). Pass empty string to skip a slope type. Requires the obstacle map to be created first.

slopeLeftIds.name: Slope left IDs
slopeLeftIds.desc: Comma-separated tile IDs for 45° slope left (/)

slopeRightIds.name: Slope right IDs
slopeRightIds.desc: Comma-separated tile IDs for 45° slope right (\)

gentleLeftIds.name: Gentle left IDs
gentleLeftIds.desc: Comma-separated tile IDs for 22.5° gentle slope left (/)

gentleRightIds.name: Gentle right IDs
gentleRightIds.desc: Comma-separated tile IDs for 22.5° gentle slope right (\)

MarkSlopeRegion.description: Mark a diagonal region of tiles as slope. Specify the start and end grid corners. All tiles along the diagonal will be marked as slope with the given direction.

ScanJumpThruObjectsIntoObstacleMap.list-name: Scan jump-thru objects into obstacle map
ScanJumpThruObjectsIntoObstacleMap.description: Scan one-way platform objects into the obstacle map as jump-thru cells. Requires an existing obstacle map (call BuildObstacleMapFromLayout first). Objects must have the Jump-thru behavior enabled.

ScanSolidObjectsIntoObstacleMap.list-name: Scan solid objects into obstacle map
ScanSolidObjectsIntoObstacleMap.description: Scan solid objects into the obstacle map. Requires an existing obstacle map (call BuildObstacleMapFromLayout first). Tilemaps are scanned cell-by-cell; sprites use bounding box. Objects must have the Solid behavior enabled.

solidObjects.name: Solid objects
solidObjects.desc: Objects with Solid behavior enabled (tilemaps or sprites)

SetHazardRadius.description: Set the radius in tiles for circular/rectangular hazard influence. Tiles within this radius of a hazard will have their pathfinding cost increased.

SetRePathThreshold.description: Set how many tiles the character can drift from the path before automatic re-pathing triggers. Higher values = more tolerance for deviation.

SetTileHazard.description: Set the hazard severity for a specific tile. Higher values make the AI avoid this tile more strongly. 0 = no hazard. Hazard avoidance is automatically enabled when any hazard is added. Use this to mark dangerous areas like spikes or lava.

severity.name: Severity
severity.desc: Hazard severity (0 = none, higher = more dangerous)

SetTileState.description: Set the state of a tile at the specified grid coordinates. Use this to mark tiles as solid obstacles, clear space, jump-thru platforms, areas to avoid, or slopes.

SetTileStateWorld.list-name: Set tile state at world position
SetTileStateWorld.description: Set the state of a tile at the specified world coordinates. The world position is automatically converted to grid coordinates.

UsePathfindingObstacleMap.description: Use the obstacle map from the Pathfinding behavior instead of a custom map. Enable auto-regenerate to automatically rebuild the graph when the Pathfinding map changes.

autoRegen.name: Auto-regenerate
autoRegen.desc: Automatically regenerate graph when Pathfinding map changes

FindPath.description: Calculate a path from the character's position to the target coordinates. Use this when you want the AI to navigate to a specific point. Requires: Navigation graph must be generated first.

correctToGround.name: Correct to ground
correctToGround.desc: Snap start/target to nearest walkable ground position

mode.name: Mode
mode.desc: Path mode: 'reach' finds a complete path or fails. 'nearest' paths as close as possible and never fails.

strict.name: Jump Positioning
strict.desc: Control how carefully the character positions itself before jumps and falls on THIS specific path. This only affects jump/fall precision during pathfinding — it does NOT affect edge walking (use Ledge Restriction for that). 'Default' uses whatever the property or SetStrictJumpPositioning action is set to. 'Strict' forces careful positioning — use for dangerous routes over pits or narrow platforms. 'Relaxed' skips positioning checks for maximum speed — use for chase sequences or when the character is fleeing and precision doesn't matter.

JumpTowardPosition.description: Immediately jump toward a target position. The character jumps from its current position with full strength, moving horizontally toward the target. No pathfinding is involved — the character simply lunges at the target. Use for: jump attacks, stomps, lunges. Triggers 'On jump toward executed' when the jump starts. The character must be on the floor to jump.

RegenerateGraph.description: Rebuild the navigation graph from scratch. Use after modifying the level layout, adding/removing obstacles, or changing platform positions.

SetAutoControl.description: Toggle auto-movement on/off. When enabled, the behavior automatically controls the Platform behavior to follow paths. When disabled, you control movement yourself using path data expressions.

SetCoyoteTime.description: Set the coyote time window in seconds. The AI can jump within this window after walking off a ledge. Set to 0 to disable coyote time.

SetLedgeLeniency.description: Set how many pixels past a platform edge the AI can walk before stopping (0 = strict stop). Increase for more natural-looking patrol movement near edges. Only used when ledge restriction is enabled.

pixels.name: Pixels
pixels.desc: Pixels past ledge edge before stopping

SetLedgeRestriction.description: Prevents AI characters from walking off platform edges when they have no reason to leave. Useful for patrol guards that should stay on their platform, or NPCs that shouldn't wander off rooftops. This only stops characters from casually walking off edges — if the AI's path requires a jump or fall to reach its goal, it will still leave the platform. To make those jumps and falls more precise, use 'Set strict jump positioning' instead.

SetPathStrategy.description: Change how the AI picks the best route when multiple paths exist. Balanced: weighs distance and difficulty equally. Shortest Distance: always takes the fastest route. Safest Route: avoids jumps and falls. Simplest Path: fewest waypoints.

SetRePathCooldown.description: Set the minimum time in seconds between automatic re-path attempts. Lower values = more responsive re-pathing but more CPU usage. Default is 0.5 seconds.

SetStrictJumpPositioning.description: Toggle whether this AI character slows down and carefully positions itself before jumping or falling during pathfinding. This does NOT affect walking off edges (use 'Set ledge restriction' for that). Use this to change behavior at runtime — for example, disable when a boss enters 'rage mode' for reckless movement, or enable when an NPC needs to carefully cross a narrow bridge. Overrides the property setting for this character.

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.desc: Enable or disable strict jump positioning

StopPathfinding.description: Stop the character immediately and clear the current path. Use when you want to cancel AI navigation and regain manual control.

SetMaxPathsPerTick.display-text: Set max paths per tick to {0}
SetMaxPathsPerTick.description: Limit path calculations per tick to prevent frame drops with many agents. 0 = unlimited (default). Re-paths always run immediately regardless of this limit.

count.name: Max paths
count.desc: Maximum path calculations per tick (0 = unlimited)

AddElevatorStop.display-text: Add elevator stop to group {0} at ({1}, {2}) [Speed: {3}]
AddElevatorStop.description: Add a stop to an elevator group. Automatically creates two-way gradual portals between this stop and all other stops in the same group. Cost is auto-calculated from distance and speed. Use a unique group name (e.g. 'elevator_A') for each elevator. Example: 3 calls with the same group creates 3 pairwise portals (Floor1-Floor2, Floor1-Floor3, Floor2-Floor3). Use PortalExitX/PortalExitY in 'On portal entry' to determine which floor the AI is heading to.

groupId.name: Group
groupId.desc: Unique group name for this elevator (e.g. 'elevator_A')

x.name: X
x.desc: World X position of this stop

y.name: Y
y.desc: World Y position of this stop

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Movement speed in pixels per second

AddElevatorStopFromObject.display-text: Add elevator stop to group {0} at {1} [Speed: {2}]
AddElevatorStopFromObject.description: Add an elevator stop using an object's position. Same as 'Add elevator stop' but uses the object's current X/Y. The object serves as a floor marker.

groupId.name: Group
groupId.desc: Unique group name for this elevator

object.name: Object
object.desc: The object to use as the elevator stop position

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Movement speed in pixels per second

AddGradualPortal.description: Add a portal that gradually moves the AI from entry to exit at the given speed. The character moves in a straight line (any direction — vertical, horizontal, or diagonal). Platform behavior is disabled during movement. Use for: elevators, lifts, moving platforms, ziplines. For vertical-only movement (ladders/ropes), align entry and exit X positions, or use 'Pause at portal' to implement your own custom movement via events.

direction.name: Direction
direction.desc: One-way: entry to exit only. Two-way: works in both directions.

entryX.name: Entry X
entryX.desc: Entry world X position in pixels

entryY.name: Entry Y
entryY.desc: Entry world Y position in pixels

exitX.name: Exit X
exitX.desc: Exit world X position in pixels

exitY.name: Exit Y
exitY.desc: Exit world Y position in pixels

cost.name: Cost
cost.desc: Movement cost. Default 1 = auto-calculated from distance and speed. Set higher to make AI avoid this portal.

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Movement speed in pixels per second

AddGradualPortalFromObjects.description: Add a gradual portal using two objects. Character moves from entry object to exit object at the given speed. Use for: linking elevator sprites, rope endpoints, etc.

direction.name: Direction
direction.desc: One-way: entry to exit only. Two-way: works in both directions.

entryObject.name: Entry object
entryObject.desc: The object to use as the portal entry point

exitObject.name: Exit object
exitObject.desc: The object to use as the portal exit point

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Movement speed in pixels per second

AddInstantPortal.description: Add a portal that instantly teleports the AI from the entry to the exit. Use for: teleporters, doors, warp zones, or any portal where the character disappears and reappears at the exit. Use 'On portal entry' with 'Pause at portal' to play animations before the teleport happens.

direction.name: Direction
direction.desc: One-way: entry to exit only. Two-way: works in both directions.

entryX.name: Entry X
entryX.desc: Entry world X position in pixels

entryY.name: Entry Y
entryY.desc: Entry world Y position in pixels

exitX.name: Exit X
exitX.desc: Exit world X position in pixels

exitY.name: Exit Y
exitY.desc: Exit world Y position in pixels

cost.name: Cost
cost.desc: How much the AI 'pays' to use this portal. Default 1 = same as walking one tile. Lower = preferred, higher = avoided.

AddInstantPortalFromObjects.description: Add an instant portal using two objects as entry and exit positions. The objects' current X/Y positions are used. Use for: linking door sprites, warp pad objects, etc.

direction.name: Direction
direction.desc: One-way: entry to exit only. Two-way: works in both directions.

entryObject.name: Entry object
entryObject.desc: The object to use as the portal entry point

exitObject.name: Exit object
exitObject.desc: The object to use as the portal exit point

ClearAllPortals.description: Remove all portals from the navigation graph. Useful when resetting the level or switching layouts.

CompletePortal.description: Finish a paused portal without executing its built-in movement. Use this when you've already moved the character yourself (e.g., custom animation, physics launch, manual position set). The AI will continue pathfinding from wherever the character is now. Also works mid-traverse to cut a gradual portal short.

PauseAtPortal.description: Call INSIDE 'On portal entry' to pause the AI before the portal executes. The character stops at the entry point and waits. Use this to play animations, open doors, trigger screen transitions, or run any custom events before the portal activates. Call 'Resume portal' to execute the built-in behavior, or 'Complete portal' if you moved the character yourself.

RemovePortal.description: Remove a portal by its ID. The portal connection is removed from the navigation graph immediately.

portalId.name: Portal ID
portalId.desc: The ID of the portal to remove

RemovePortalAtObject.description: Remove the portal closest to this object. Works with both entry and exit positions — for two-way portals, either endpoint object can be used.

object.name: Object
object.desc: The object whose position to match against portal positions

ResumePortal.description: Continue portal execution after pausing with 'Pause at portal'. For instant portals: teleports the character to the exit. For gradual portals: begins moving the character toward the exit. Use this when you want the portal's built-in movement to handle the transition.

SetPortalCost.description: Change how 'expensive' a portal is for the AI to use. Lower cost = preferred, higher cost = avoided.

portalId.name: Portal ID
portalId.desc: The ID of the portal to configure

SetPortalIgnoreHazards.description: Set whether a portal ignores nearby hazards when calculating its pathfinding cost.

portalId.name: Portal ID
portalId.desc: The ID of the portal to configure

ignoreHazards.name: Ignore hazards
ignoreHazards.desc: Whether this portal should ignore hazards

SetPortalSpeed.description: Change the movement speed of a gradual portal (pixels per second). Has no effect on instant portals.

portalId.name: Portal ID
portalId.desc: The ID of the portal to configure

speed.name: Speed
speed.desc: Movement speed in pixels per second

TeleportToPosition.description: Instantly move the character to the given position. Can be used anywhere — inside portal events, on button press, on collision, etc. Suppresses re-pathing for one tick to prevent the AI from thinking it's lost. Useful with 'Pause at portal' + 'Complete portal' for fully custom portal behavior.

x.name: X
x.desc: Target world X position in pixels

y.name: Y
y.desc: Target world Y position in pixels

SetMultiAgentAvoidance.description: Enable or disable multi-agent collision avoidance. When enabled, AI agents will attempt to avoid paths occupied by other agents. Shared Navigation graph mode only — requires graph mode set to 'shared'.

IsNodeLedge.description: Check if a specific node is marked as a ledge (platform edge). Returns true if the node is a left or right ledge.

IsPositionHazardous.description: Check if a specific world position is within any hazard area (circle, rect, or tile). Returns true if any hazard affects this position.

IsSettingUpPathfinding.description: Check if the behavior is currently waiting for the Pathfinding obstacle map to initialize. Returns true during async setup.

OnObstacleMapCreated.description: Triggered when a custom obstacle map is successfully created. Use this to start configuring tiles after map creation.

OnObstacleMapRemoved.description: Triggered when the obstacle map is cleared or removed. Use this to clean up related data or reset systems.

OnPathfindingMapFailed.description: Triggered when the Pathfinding behavior's obstacle map fails to initialize. Use this to implement fallback error handling.

OnPathfindingMapReady.description: Triggered when the Pathfinding behavior's obstacle map is ready for use. Use this to start graph generation after Pathfinding initialization.

OnPathfindingMapTimeout.description: Triggered when waiting for the Pathfinding obstacle map times out. Use this to handle slow or stuck initialization.

TileHasState.description: Check if a tile at the given grid position has the specified state. Use this to query tile properties before actions.

TileHasStateWorld.list-name: Tile has state at world position
TileHasStateWorld.description: Check if a tile at the given world position has the specified state. World coordinates are automatically converted to grid coordinates.

HasPath.description: Check if the character currently has an active pathfinding path. Returns true while navigating, false when idle or path is complete.

IsAtIsland.description: Check if the character is standing on a single-tile platform (isolated platform). Use this to detect precarious positions or trigger special behaviors.

IsAtLedge.description: Check if the character is currently standing on a ledge node (edge of a platform). Use this to trigger ledge-specific behaviors or animations.

IsPlatformEnabled.description: Check if the associated Platform behavior is currently enabled. Returns false if Platform behavior is disabled or not found.

NodeExistsGrid.description: Check if a navigation node exists at the specified grid coordinates. Use this to validate positions before pathfinding or placing objects.

NodeExistsWorld.description: Check if a navigation node exists at the specified world coordinates. Use this to validate world positions before pathfinding.

OnGraphGenerated.description: Triggered when the navigation graph has been successfully generated. Use this to start pathfinding operations after map setup.

OnJumpTowardLaunched.description: Triggered when the 'Jump toward position' action launches the character. Use this to play attack animations, spawn effects, or apply damage. The target position is available via JumpTowardTargetX/Y expressions.

OnPathComplete.description: Triggered when the AI arrives at the final destination. Use this to trigger arrival animations, next actions, or goal completion logic.

OnPathFailed.description: Triggered when pathfinding fails to find a valid path to the target. Use this to handle unreachable destinations or implement fallback behaviors.

OnPathFound.description: Triggered when a path has been successfully calculated. Use this to start custom actions when pathfinding succeeds.

OnRePathTriggered.description: Triggered when automatic re-pathing occurs due to the character drifting too far from the path. Use this to monitor navigation accuracy.

OnWaypointReached.description: Triggered each time the character reaches a waypoint along the path. Use this to play footstep sounds, particle effects, or update animations.

OnWaypointStuck.description: Triggered when the character has been stuck at a waypoint for too long (exceeds Max Waypoint Time). The path is automatically cancelled. Use this to handle stuck situations or repath.

IsPathPending.description: True when a path request is queued and waiting to be processed (time-slicing is active and the per-tick budget was reached).

IsAtPortal.description: True when the AI is paused at a portal entry (after 'Pause at portal' was called but before 'Resume portal' or 'Complete portal'). Use to check if the character is waiting at a portal.

IsTraversingPortal.description: True when the AI is currently moving through a gradual portal (elevator, ladder, etc.). Platform behavior is disabled during traversal.

OnPortalComplete.description: Triggered when portal execution finishes — after an instant teleport completes, a gradual movement reaches the exit, or 'Complete portal' is called. Use this for post-portal effects like opening doors at the exit, playing arrival animations, etc.

OnPortalEntry.description: Triggered when the AI arrives at a portal entry point, BEFORE the portal executes. Use 'Pause at portal' inside this event to delay execution and run your own events first (animations, sounds, screen effects). If you don't pause, the portal executes immediately. Use CurrentPortalID to identify which portal was reached.

IsMultiAgentAvoidanceEnabled.description: Check if multi-agent collision avoidance is currently enabled. Shared Navigation graph mode only — requires graph mode set to 'shared'.

CalculatedJumpDistance.description: Get the calculated maximum horizontal jump distance in pixels based on Platform behavior settings. Used for determining reachable positions.

CalculatedJumpHeight.description: Get the calculated maximum jump height in pixels based on Platform behavior settings. Used for determining reachable positions.

PlatformJumpStrength.description: Get the jump strength from the Platform behavior. Used for internal pathfinding calculations. Returns 0 if Platform behavior not found.

PlatformMaxSpeed.description: Get the max speed from the Platform behavior. Used for internal pathfinding calculations. Returns 0 if Platform behavior not found.

IsNodeIsland.description: Check if a node at grid coordinates is an island (single-tile platform). Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or node doesn't exist.

IsNodeLeftLedge.description: Check if a node at grid coordinates is a left ledge. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or node doesn't exist.

IsNodeRightLedge.description: Check if a node at grid coordinates is a right ledge. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or node doesn't exist.

IsTileJumpThru.description: Check if a tile at grid coordinates is a jump-thru platform. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or tile doesn't exist.

NearestNodeGridX.description: Get the grid X coordinate of the nearest navigation node to a world position. Returns -1 if no nodes exist.

NearestNodeGridY.description: Get the grid Y coordinate of the nearest navigation node to a world position. Returns -1 if no nodes exist.

NearestNodeX.description: Get the world X position of the nearest navigation node to a world position. Returns 0 if no nodes exist.

NearestNodeY.description: Get the world Y position of the nearest navigation node to a world position. Returns 0 if no nodes exist.

NodeAtIndexConnectionCount.description: Get the number of connections (edges) from a node by its index. Returns 0 if index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexGridX.description: Get the grid X coordinate of a node by its index in the node array. Returns -1 if index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexGridY.description: Get the grid Y coordinate of a node by its index in the node array. Returns -1 if index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexIsLeftLedge.description: Check if a node is a left ledge by its index. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexIsRightLedge.description: Check if a node is a right ledge by its index. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexIsSlope.description: Check if a node is on a slope by its index. Returns 1 if true, 0 if false or index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexX.description: Get the world X position of a node by its index in the node array. Returns 0 if index is out of bounds.

NodeAtIndexY.description: Get the world Y position of a node by its index in the node array. Returns 0 if index is out of bounds.

NodeConnectionAction.description: Get the action name for a connection (e.g., 'walk', 'jump', 'fall'). Returns empty string if node/connection doesn't exist.

NodeConnectionCost.description: Get the movement cost for a connection. Returns 0 if node/connection doesn't exist.

NodeConnectionCount.description: Get the number of connections (edges) from a node at grid coordinates. Returns 0 if node doesn't exist.

NodeConnectionTargetX.description: Get the world X position of a connection's target node. Returns 0 if node/connection doesn't exist.

NodeConnectionTargetY.description: Get the world Y position of a connection's target node. Returns 0 if node/connection doesn't exist.

HazardCount.description: Get the total number of active hazards (circles and rectangles). Does not include tile hazards.

HazardSeverity.description: Get the total hazard severity at a world position from all sources (circles, rects, tiles). Higher values = more dangerous.

PositionIsHazardous.description: Check if a world position is hazardous. Returns 1 if hazardous, 0 if safe.

TileHazardSeverity.description: Get the hazard severity of a specific tile. Returns 0 if no hazard. Only checks tile-based hazards, not circles/rects.

GridHeight.description: Get the height of the obstacle map in tiles. Returns 0 if no map exists.

GridTileSize.description: Get the tile size in pixels. Returns 0 if no map exists.

GridWidth.description: Get the width of the obstacle map in tiles. Returns 0 if no map exists.

HazardRadius.description: Get the current hazard radius setting in tiles. This affects how far hazard influence spreads.

ObstacleMapJSON.description: Get the current obstacle map as a JSON string. Use this to save the map to local storage or export to files.

ObstacleMapSource.description: Get the source of the current obstacle map. Returns 'custom', 'pathfinding', or 'none'.

RePathCooldown.description: Get the current re-path cooldown in seconds. This is the minimum time between automatic re-path attempts.

RePathThreshold.description: Get the current re-path threshold in tiles. This is how far the character can drift before automatic re-pathing triggers.

SlopeDirection.description: Get the slope direction of a tile at the specified grid coordinates. Returns 'left', 'right', or empty string if not a slope.

TileState.description: Get the state of a tile at the specified grid coordinates. Returns 'solid', 'clear', 'jump-thru', 'avoid', 'slope-left', 'slope-right', or empty string if out of bounds.

WaitTickCount.description: Get the number of ticks spent waiting for the Pathfinding obstacle map to initialize. Used for debugging timeout issues.

WorldToGridX.description: Convert a world X position to grid X coordinate. Returns the grid tile number at the given pixel position.

WorldToGridY.description: Convert a world Y position to grid Y coordinate. Returns the grid tile number at the given pixel position.

AngleToWaypoint.description: Get the angle in degrees from the character to the current waypoint. Returns 0 if no path is active.

CoyoteTime.description: Get the current coyote time setting in seconds. This is the window after walking off a ledge where jumps are still allowed.

CoyoteTimer.description: Get the current coyote timer value in seconds. This counts down after leaving the ground. Returns 0 when on ground or timer expired.

CurrentPathAction.description: Get the action name for a waypoint by index (e.g., 'walk', 'jump', 'fall', 'portal'). Returns empty string if index is out of bounds.

CurrentWaypoint.description: Get the index of the current waypoint the character is moving toward. Returns -1 if no path is active.

CurrentWaypointX.description: Get the world X position of the current waypoint. Returns 0 if no path is active.

CurrentWaypointY.description: Get the world Y position of the current waypoint. Returns 0 if no path is active.

DistanceToWaypoint.description: Get the distance in pixels from the character to the current waypoint. Returns 0 if no path is active.

EstimatedVelocityX.description: Get the estimated horizontal velocity needed to follow the current path. Returns 0 if no path is active.

JumpTowardTargetX.description: Get the world X position of the jump-at target. Returns 0 if not in jump-at mode.

JumpTowardTargetY.description: Get the world Y position of the jump-at target. Returns 0 if not in jump-at mode.

LedgeLeniency.description: Get the ledge leniency setting in pixels. This is how far past a ledge edge the AI can walk before stopping.

LedgeRestriction.description: Get whether ledge restriction is enabled. Returns 1 if enabled, 0 if disabled.

NodeCount.description: Get the total number of navigation nodes in the generated graph. Returns 0 if no graph exists.

NodeWorldX.description: Get the world X position of a node at the specified grid coordinates. the node position is centred within the tile. Returns 0 if node doesn't exist.

NodeWorldY.description: Get the world Y position of a node at the specified grid coordinates. the node position is centred within the tile. Returns 0 if node doesn't exist.

PathCost.description: Get the total calculated cost of the current path. Returns 0 if no path is active.

PathFailReason.description: Get the reason the last pathfinding attempt failed. Returns: 'no_start_node', 'no_goal_node', 'max_nodes_reached', 'no_path', or empty string if path succeeded.

PathStrategy.description: Get the current path strategy preset (balanced, shortest, safest, simplest).

PathTargetGridX.description: Get the grid X coordinate of the path target. Returns -1 if no path is active.

PathTargetGridY.description: Get the grid Y coordinate of the path target. Returns -1 if no path is active.

PathTargetX.description: Get the world X position of the path target. Pass 'original' for raw input or 'corrected' for ground-snapped position.

PathTargetY.description: Get the world Y position of the path target. Pass 'original' for raw input or 'corrected' for ground-snapped position.

StoppingDistance.description: Get the calculated stopping distance in pixels based on the Platform behavior's current speed. Used for waypoint arrival detection.

StrictJumpPositioning.description: Get whether strict jump positioning is currently active for this character. Returns 1 if enabled, 0 if disabled. Useful for conditional logic — e.g. switching between careful and aggressive pathfinding modes.

WaypointCount.description: Get the total number of waypoints in the current path. Returns 0 if no path is active.

WaypointGridX.description: Get the grid X coordinate of a waypoint by index. Returns -1 if index is out of bounds.

WaypointGridY.description: Get the grid Y coordinate of a waypoint by index. Returns -1 if index is out of bounds.

WaypointX.description: Get the world X position of a waypoint by index. the waypoint position is centred within the tile. Returns 0 if index is out of bounds.

WaypointY.description: Get the world Y position of a waypoint by index. the waypoint position is centred within the tile. Returns 0 if index is out of bounds.

MaxPathsPerTick.description: Current max paths per tick limit (0 = unlimited).

PathQueueSize.description: Number of path requests currently waiting in the queue.

CurrentPortalID.description: Returns the portal ID during OnPortalEntry/OnPortalComplete triggers. Use to identify which portal was reached.

LastPortalID.description: Returns the ID of the most recently added portal. Use right after adding a portal to save the ID for later configuration or removal.

PortalCount.description: Get the total number of portals.

PortalExitX.description: Get the exit X position of the current portal. Valid inside OnPortalEntry/OnPortalComplete triggers.

PortalExitY.description: Get the exit Y position of the current portal. Valid inside OnPortalEntry/OnPortalComplete triggers.

PortalProgress.description: Get the 0-1 traversal progress for gradual portals. Returns 0 if not traversing.

PortalType.description: Returns 'instant' or 'gradual' for the given portal ID.

NearbyAgentCount.description: Get the number of nearby AI agents within detection range. Used for multi-agent avoidance calculations. Returns 0 if multi-agent avoidance is disabled. Shared Navigation graph mode only — requires graph mode set to 'shared'.
